i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-x\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nx = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-y\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            ny = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-z\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nz = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    if (ny == 0) ny = nx;\n    if (nz == 0) nz = nx;\n    \n    printf(\"3D Stencil Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Grid size: %zu x %zu x %zu\\n\", nx, ny, nz);\n    printf(\"Iterations: %d\\n\", iterations);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    size_t gridSize = nx * ny * nz;\n    \n    // Allocate grids (double buffering)\n    std::vector<Real> grid1(gridSize);\n    std::vector<Real> grid2(gridSize);\n    \n    // Initialize\n    printf(\"Initializing grid...\\n\");\n    initializeGrid(grid1, nx, ny, nz);\n    \n    // Run stencil iterations\n    printf(\"Running stencil computation...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    for (int iter = 0; iter < iterations; ++iter) {\n        if (iter % 2 == 0) {\n            stencilIteration(grid1, grid2, nx, ny, nz);\n        } else {\n            stencilIteration(grid2, grid1, nx, ny, nz);\n        }\n    }\n    \n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n    \n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n    \n    // Calculate performance metrics\n    double cellUpdates = (double)((nx-2) * (ny-2) * (nz-2)) * iterations;\n    double mcups = cellUpdates / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e6; x + 1 < nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t idx = base + x;\n                const Real center = in[idx];\n                const Real left = in[idx - 1];\n                const Real right = in[idx + 1];\n                const Real front = in[idx - nx];\n                const Real back = in[idx + nx];\n                const Real bottom = in[idx - nx * ny];\n                const Real top = in[idx + nx * ny];\n\n                out[idx] = (center + left + right + front + back + bottom + top) / 7.0;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(std::span<const Real> grid, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nx, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t ny, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nz) {\n    // Simple sanity checks\n\n    // 1.  // Will be set to nx if not specified\n    size_t nz = 0;  // Will be set to nx if not specified\n    int iterations = 10;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; Left uninitialized so that the first\n    // touch happens in the parallel initialization below, not on one thread.\n    auto grid1Storage = std::make_unique_for_overwrite<Real[]>(gridSize);\n    auto grid2Storage = std::make_unique_for_overwrite<Real[]>(gridSize);\n    const std::span<Real> grid1(grid1Storage.get(), gridSize);\n    const std::span<Real> grid2(grid2Storage.get(), gridSize);\n\n    // Initialize\n    printf(\"Initializing grid...\\n\");\n    initializeGrid(grid1, nx, ny, nz);\n    // grid2 is fully overwritten by the first iteration before it is read; this\n    // only first-touches its pages on the worker threads outside the timed region.\n    initializeGrid(grid2, nx, ny, nz);\n\n    // Run stencil iterations\n    printf(\"Running stencil computation...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    for (int iter = 0; iter < iterations; ++iter) {\n        if (iter % 2 == 0) {\n            stencilIteration(grid1, grid2, nx, ny, nz);\n        } else {\n            stencilIteration(grid2, grid1, nx, ny, nz);\n        }\n    }\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n    // Calculate performance metrics\n    double cellUpdates = (double)((nx-2) * (ny-2) * (nz-2)) * iterations;\n    double mcups = cellUpdates / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e6;  // Million cell updates per second\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f MCellUpdates/s\\n\", mcups);\n\n    // Print results for external validation\n    const std::span<Real> finalGrid = (iterations % 2 == 0) ? {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfxLW3QTaEEyGHJsvjg4T","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The stencil3d benchmark now runs with OpenMP unconditionally. Output is byte-identical to the original serial program, and a 256³ run reaches about 21× the original throughput at 32 threads.\n\n**Changes (only `stencil3d/stencil3d.cpp` and `stencil3d/CMakeLists.txt`):**\n\n- **Parallel loops:** the grid initialization, the stencil sweep, and the validation scans use `#pragma omp parallel for`. The stencil and initialization both split work over `(z, y)` rows with `schedule(static)`, so each thread reuses the same rows across iterations.\n- **Boundary handling:** the separate boundary-copy pass is folded into the row loop. Boundary rows are copied with `std::copy`, and interior rows copy their two x-edge cells and compute the rest. Each cell is written once per iteration.\n- **Same arithmetic:** the 7-point sum keeps the original operation order, so results match bit-for-bit.\n- **NUMA first touch:** the grids are allocated with `std::make_unique_for_overwrite` instead of `std::vector`, so the parallel init touches the pages rather than one thread zeroing them. `grid2` is also initialized before timing; the first iteration overwrites all of it, so this is safe.\n- **Validation:** the NaN/Inf check is a parallel count, and min/max use OpenMP reductions. The reported range and pass/fail logic are unchanged.\n- **CMake:** `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX` are linked. The executable name and the existing flags are unchanged.\n\n**Verification:**\n- Built with g++ 13.2 with no warnings under `-Wall -Wextra`.\n- Compared against a serial build of the original across nine configurations, including non-cubic grids, `nx` = 1, 2, 3, and 0 iterations. Each ran at 1, 4, 16, and 256 threads. Exit codes and all output lines (including the FNV hash and sampled values) match, excluding the timing lines.\n- Throughput at 256³, 20 iterations (AMD EPYC 7763, 2 NUMA nodes):\n\n| Threads | MCellUpdates/s |\n|---|---|\n| Original (serial) | 410 |\n| 1 | 1008 |\n| 4 | 3344 |\n| 16 | 8194 |\n| 32 | 8858 |\n\nScaling flattens past 16 threads, which is likely memory bandwidth. Thread pinning (`OMP_PROC_BIND`/`OMP_PLACES`) is left to the environment and was not tuned here.\n\n**Choices I made:**\n- Left the `common/` headers untouched. `print_results` still runs serially; it is only called with `-r` after timing.\n- With `-r`, the final grid is copied into a `std::vector` for `print_results`. That copy happens after timing.\n- Left the pre-existing `nx-2`-style size_t underflow in the MCUPS calculation as-is, since it is outside the parallel work."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":366,"cache_read_input_tokens":32388,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":366},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"4c593f56-ed7e-400d-b9fe-841b87ab53ec","uuid":"70ca12fc-0d1b-4907-83bd-30451a1c0fca","timestamp":"2026-10-12T12:23:55.132Z","request_id":"req_011CfxLW37rBuzXNieUabcnx"}
